claims.content: The Customer wants to browse and search active auction products by product attributes, structured filters such as Retail Category, Gemstone, Product Type, Brand, Material Purity, and Buyer, or full-text description in order to locate products of interest.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to browse and search active auction products by product attributes, structured filters such as Retail Category, Gemstone, Product Type, Brand, Material Purity, and Buyer, or full-text description in order to locate products of interest.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer browses or searches active auction products using product attributes, structured drop-down filters, or full-text description and locates matching products.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer decides to browse or search products.
scope_contract.success_boundary: Matching active auction products are found or identified in the browse/search results.
in_scope_actions: search for active auction items by product attributes
excluded_adjacent_actions: Auctioneer editing currently running or scheduled auctions
variant_dimensions: structured filters such as Retail Category, Gemstone, Product Type, Brand, Material Purity, and Buyer

system state requirements for product eligibility
system state: Auctioneer role active and authorized
feature availability: Create New Auctions Page accessible for daily use

claims.content: The Customer initiates the use case by clicking a product category or by entering search criteria or a keyword/item number and activating the corresponding SEARCH, Go, or Find Product control.
The Customer navigates from the Home Page to Catalog Pages.

From the Catalog Pages, the Customer accesses the product search interface, which includes scrolling list boxes for Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone Type, Material Type, Material Purity, and Brand.

The Customer selects a product category to browse or specifies search criteria using product attributes, structured drop-down filters such as Retail Category, Gemstone, Product Type, Brand, Material Purity, and Buyer, or a full-text description.

The Customer activates the corresponding browse/search control (for example, by clicking a product category, the SEARCH button, the Go button, or the Find Product button) to submit the selected category or search criteria.

The system searches active auction items that match the selected category, attributes, structured filters, or full-text description; active auction items are searchable by all item attributes and by full-text search on the description field.
The system finds multiple matching active auction items and loads the category/search result page using the default catalog view.

The system displays a table titled 'Search Results' with sortable column headers (Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, Increment) populated with matching auction items, including product image thumbnail, bid values, timing, duration, type, and increment amount.
The Customer identifies matching active auction products in the displayed browse/search results.

covered_aspect_ids: detailed user actions within pages (selecting filters, clicking items)
system response details for successful searches

claims.content: Diverges from Step 3: As an alternative to selecting a product category or entering a full-text description, the Customer specifies search criteria using structured drop-down filters, including Retail Category, Product Type, Auction Type, Gemstone, Gemstone Color, Metal Purity, Brand, Dimensions, Optical Properties, Size, Carat Weight, Current Bid, Hot Buys, Birthstone, Department, Shape, Style, Length, and Country.
Diverges from Step 3: The Customer searches for a specific product by entering its Product ID (e.g., 'ABC123') in the 'Search by Product ID' field and activating the 'Go' button.
Diverges from Step 6: If the search results in only one match, the system loads the product details page instead of the category/search result page.

Diverges from Step 6: Instead of the default Catalog View, the Customer chooses List View, which displays items horizontally and includes a SmartBid button in addition to the standard module elements.

covered_aspect_ids: alternative_flow: single match redirects to product details
alternative_flow: navigate to bidder history from results
alternative_flow: apply profile to selected items

claims.content: At main_flow Step 5, if the Customer's search or browse action yields zero matching active auction products, the system displays a 'No Results Found' page containing a message that no matches were found, a 'Search Tips' section with five actionable suggestions to refine the search (for example, checking for typos and removing unnecessary words), a 'May We Suggest' section with static lists of popular gemstone and jewelry searches, and a dynamically updated list of popular search terms/phrases using Omniture data.
At main_flow Step 3, if the Customer clicks a menu bar link that contains no product (for example, a collectibles link), the system serves a 'no results found' page.

At main_flow Step 5, if an active auction product matches the search criteria but lacks an available image, that product is excluded from search results, catalog pages, and product details pages and therefore does not appear in the visible result set.

claims.content: After successful search execution, the system displays a table titled 'Search Results' with sortable column headers (Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, Increment) populated with matching auction items.
Each row in the displayed Search Results table shows the product image thumbnail, bid values, timing, duration, type, and increment amount for the matching auction item.
When multiple matching items are found, the category/search result page is loaded using the default catalog view.
